comments.text: 100m Slither's entry, jumped to by the resident event loader at $0970. Silences the sound through the resident $C540, banks the KERNAL and BASIC ROMs out (I/O stays), points the NMI vector at $30B8 and the IRQ vector at irq_entry ($0D6F), stops CIA 1's timer interrupt and turns on the raster interrupt at line 256, picks video bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF) with the screen at $4000 and the character set at $4800, turns on all eight sprites and blacks the border. Then clears the screen ($105C), and falls into race_restart.

The top of each race: resets the crowd speed ($0E = 6) and the race state ($0CA3 and the set-up calls), lets the worms idle, then asks each worm in turn to press fire (message 0 or 1 through show_message $26A8, then wait_ready $0CE9). Which device answered for each worm is kept at $0D60 and $0D61: a keyboard player with joystick two is refused (message 6), and when one device answered for both worms worm one, on the far track, is run by the computer (message 4, "COMPUTER PACE MAKER ON FAR TRACK"). Then shows "PREPARE TO RACE", waits 100 x 256 input polls or a fire press (wait_or_fire $0C65), starts the countdown ($0C8F), starts the clock and runs the per-frame race loop: wait for raster line 256, then update both worms, the panels and the clock, until race_check ($12F8) sets $1405 to 2.

The race clock in BCD, hundredths ($0C28) and seconds ($0C29); the copy draw_time takes at the finish ($0C2A/$0C2B); the two worms' best times ($0C2C-$0C2F, $99 99 when none); the pace-maker-beaten flag ($0C30); the clock-running flag ($0C31); and $0C32.
The race clock's seconds, in BCD.
The finishing time's hundredths, copied by draw_time.
The finishing time's seconds, copied by draw_time.
Worm one's best time, hundredths then seconds ($99 99 when none).
Worm one's best time, seconds byte (check_record reads it as $0C2C + 1).
Set when worm one, the pace-maker, has been beaten; quit_to_menu passes it on at $B809.
The clock-running flag: the interrupt adds to the clock while it is set.
Cleared at the start of each race; nothing reads it.

Every $0E frames (6 normally, 4 once a worm has finished), rotates four 40-character rows of the stand on the screen ($4118, $4140, $4168, $4190 and $41B8, rows 7 to 11) one row along, so the crowd seems to move.
crowd_cycle's frame count ($0C63) and the frame counter the interrupt adds one to ($0C64).
The frame counter the interrupt adds one to.
Waits about A x 256 polls of the fire buttons (fire_device $0D2C), returning early when one is pressed. A, X and Y are kept.
Where wait_or_fire keeps X and Y.
wait_or_fire's saved Y.
Waits until a fire button is pressed (fire_device). A is kept. No caller in this event.
Starts sound or speech 1 through $2C48 (A=1, X=2), waits until $2C15 says it has finished, then starts 2: the start signal before the clock runs.

Clears the race clock ($0C28-$0C2B), stops it ($0C31 = 0), clears the colon flag $1484 and the sprites' ninth X bits, and puts both worms back on the start line: position $01C0 (low byte $2917, high byte $2919), $291B = $24, $2925 = $20, frame $0B ($2076) and screen X $89 ($2913), with their speed and state bytes $291D, $291F and $2923 cleared.

Asks worm A (0 or 1) to press fire: blinks its sprites by switching its frame ($2076) between its own and $FF (hidden) every five frames, until fire_device reports a press. Stores the device that answered (0 keyboard, 1 joystick one, 2 joystick two) at $0D60 + A and shows the worm again.
wait_ready's saved frame ($0D29) and worm number ($0D2A), and a spare byte.
wait_ready's worm number.

Reads the three fire buttons the game accepts: the up-arrow key (keyboard row 6, column 6), joystick one's fire ($DC01 bit 4) and joystick two's fire ($DC00 bit 4). Returns carry set and A = 0, 1 or 2 for the first one held, in that order, or carry clear when none is; X is kept.

fire_device's saved X ($0D5F); the device each worm chose ($0D60, $0D61: 0 keyboard, 1 joystick one, 2 joystick two); the player count ($0D62, 2 for two players); spare bytes; the band number ($0D65) and its raster high bit ($0D66); and the three bands' raster lines and high bits ($0D67-$0D6C: $73, $B9 and 256).
The device worm one chose: 0 keyboard, 1 joystick one, 2 joystick two.
The device worm two chose.
The player count: 2 for two players, otherwise the pace-maker runs worm one.
The raster band the next interrupt handles (0 to 2).
The next band's raster line high bit ($80 or 0), kept for $D011.
The three bands' raster lines and high bits, two bytes a band: $73, $B9 and 256.
The high-bit bytes of the band table, read as $0D67 + 1.

The raster interrupt, reached through the RAM vector at $FFFE: counts frames in $0C64, saves A, X and Y in $07-$09 and goes to the band handler for this part of the screen (through $0D79, set by irq_next).
The operand of the JMP at $0D78, rewritten by irq_next before each band: the low byte of the next band handler's address.
The high byte of the next band handler's address, the second byte of that JMP's operand.
The three band handlers' addresses, in band order: irq_worm1 ($0DED), irq_worm2 ($0E02) and irq_bottom ($0D81).
The high bytes of the band handlers' addresses, read as band_handlers + 1.

The band handler that runs once a frame at the bottom of the screen: calls $30A8 and $352F, cycles the crowd colour counter $0E67 (0-15, every 4 frames), adds 2 to the race clock in BCD hundredths ($0C28-$0C29) while $0C31 says it runs, steps the waiting worms' idle animation ($0E6C), calls $2EFC, then acknowledges the interrupt through irq_next.
A band handler nothing points at: waits three empty calls, sets the background to red and ends the band through irq_next.

The band handler at the top of the track for worm one, in the far (upper) lane: unless its frame ($2076) is $FF, colours its sprites light green ($0D) and places them at $2913/$2915 through set_worm_sprites ($0E86).

The band handler at raster line $B9 for worm two, in the near (lower) lane: sets the background colour to red (2), waits for raster line $C2, then colours the second worm's sprites yellow (7) and places them at $2914/$2916, unless its frame is $FF.

Ends every band handler: acknowledges the raster interrupt, moves to the next of three bands ($0D65, 0 to 2), sets the raster line ($0D67) and its ninth bit ($0D68) for it and the handler address the IRQ will jump to ($0D7B to $0D79), restores A, X and Y and returns from the interrupt.

The colour set_worm_sprites gives a worm's own sprites ($0E66), the crowd colour count and its frame count ($0E67, $0E68), the idle-animation switch ($0E69) and the two waiting worms' hold counts ($0E6A, $0E6B).
The crowd colour count, 0 to 15.
Frames until the crowd colour count moves on.
Set while the waiting worms play their idle animation.
Each waiting worm's frames until its next idle frame.
The waiting worm's idle animation: given a frame in A, returns the next of $0B, $0F, $10 and back to $0B, with Y = the frames to hold it (5, or $FA on the frame that ends the cycle).

Builds one worm from the eight sprites: A is its frame, X and Y its screen position. The frame's record (pointer table $2078) gives each sprite's colour (6 keeps blue, any other value takes the worm's colour from $0E66), eight Y offsets added one after another to Y, eight X offsets added one after another to X, and the eight sprite pointers written to $43F8-$43FF.

Draws one seven-segment digit for the clock: A is the segment mask (from $1407), X and Y the screen address. Each pair of segments becomes one character code (0 to $1F, the LCD glyphs of the character set) in a 2 x 3 block of cells.
seg_digit's work byte.
Fills the screen at $4000-$43FF with spaces ($20) and colour RAM with white (1).
Waits for the raster to leave and come back to line 256: one frame.

Draws worm X's finishing time in large digits beside its panel (screen $4055 for worm one, $406E for worm two): copies the clock to $0C2A/$0C2B and writes each of the four BCD digits as a top and bottom character from the pair table at $110C, with a dot ($46) after the seconds.
The large-digit table for draw_time: ten pairs of character codes, the top and bottom halves of the digits 0 to 9.
The bottom halves of the large digits, read as time_digits + 1.

Compares worm Y's finishing time with its best ($0C2C + 2Y) and keeps the faster; when worm one beats its best in a one-player race, $0C30 records that the pace-maker's time was beaten. Plays the finish fanfare, effect $0D on voice 3, for the first worm home ($1406).
Draws the 11 x 3 block of characters at $11ED, $11F8 and $1203, coloured from $122F, $123A and $1245, over worm X's panel (screen $4029 or $4042): the sign shown when the worm has finished.
The FINISH TIME sign's characters, three rows of eleven (top $11ED, middle $11F8, bottom $1203), drawn by draw_finish_sign over a worm's panel.
The middle row of the FINISH TIME sign.
The bottom row of the FINISH TIME sign.
The DISQUALIFIED sign's characters, three rows of eleven (top $120E, middle $1219, bottom $1224), drawn by draw_out_signs over the panel of a worm that is out.
The middle row of the DISQUALIFIED sign.
The bottom row of the DISQUALIFIED sign.
The colours of the FINISH TIME sign's top row.
The colours of the FINISH TIME sign's middle row.
The colours of the FINISH TIME sign's bottom row.
The colours of the DISQUALIFIED sign's top row.
The colours of the DISQUALIFIED sign's middle row.
The colours of the DISQUALIFIED sign's bottom row.

For each worm whose state ($291F + X) is $82 (out of the race), draws an 11 x 3 block of characters over its TEMP and SLIME panel (screen $4029 for worm one, $4042 for worm two) from $120E, $1219 and $1224, coloured from $1250, $125B and $1266.

Once a frame: speeds the crowd up ($0E = 4) once either worm is done; when both are done, or worm one has burnt out, stops the clock, waits the count in $1404, shows message 5 ("PRESS FIRE TO RACE AGAIN") and sets $1405 to 1, then sets it to 2 on the next fire press, which restarts the race. While the race runs, ends it at 70 seconds (BCD $70 in $0C29): any worm still racing is put out ($82), the signs are drawn and message 3 ("TIME LIMIT EXCEEDED RACE TERMINATED") shown; otherwise checks each worm's position against the finish at $14A0.
Worm one has crossed the finish ($14A0): draws its finish sign, time and record check, and sets its state to $81 when it is first home, or to $80 and stops the clock when worm two is already home.
Worm two has crossed the finish, as worm1_home does for worm one: state $81 when first, $80 and the clock stopped when second.

race_check's wait before the "race again" prompt ($1404), its stage ($1405: 0 racing, 1 prompt shown, 2 restart) and the fanfare-played flag ($1406); then, from $1407, the seven-segment masks of the digits 0 to 9 for seg_digit.
race_check's stage: 0 racing, 1 prompt shown, 2 restart.
Set once the finish fanfare has played.
The seven-segment masks of the digits 0 to 9, one bit a segment, for seg_digit.

Draws the race clock, seconds ($0C29) and hundredths ($0C28), as four seven-segment digits at $4037, $4039, $403C and $403E, and blinks the colon at $4063 and $408B: shown for the first 0.70 of each second, hidden for the rest ($1484 remembers which).
Bit 7 set while draw_clock is showing the clock's colon.

Draws a TEMP bar six cells long at the screen address in $02/$03 for a value in A (0 to $30, larger values not drawn past full): one full cell (character $18) for every 8, one partial cell ($10 plus the remainder) and spaces after. Colours the six cells in colour RAM blue (6) below $0C, green (5) below $25 and red above.
temp_bar's copy of its value.
Draws a SLIME bar the same way as temp_bar for A (0 to $30), coloured red (2) below $0D and green (5) from there up.
slime_bar's copy of its value.

Redraws the TEMP and SLIME bars of each worm still racing ($291F/$2920 zero): TEMP is $30 less the worm's cooling level ($2925/$2926), at $402E or $4047; SLIME is its slime ($291B/$291C), at $407E or $4097.
Flashes worm X's two meter rows while it waits for its player: each call swaps their colour RAM between black and green ($15BB remembers which).

blink_meters' switch ($15BB); the two lanes' four-character stripe patterns ($15BC and $15C3), whose middle characters draw_lane1 and draw_lane2 rewrite; and the fine-scroll character tables ($15CA and $15D2, eight each), one entry per pixel of scroll.
The far lane pattern's first variable character.
The far lane pattern's second variable character.
The far lane pattern's third variable character.
The near lane pattern's first variable character.
The near lane pattern's second variable character.
The near lane pattern's third variable character.
The fine-scroll table for the stripe's first and third characters, one entry per pixel.
The fine-scroll table for the stripe's second character, one entry per pixel.

Draws the far (upper) lane's red-and-white divider row, worm one's, (screen $42A8, row 17) scrolled to the worm's distance ($2917/$2919 less its screen X $2913): the low three bits pick fine-scroll variants of the stripe characters ($15CA, $15D2), the next two bits which of four phases of the 4-character pattern ($15BC) starts the row, and the distance marker's two characters ($21, $22) go in at the columns marker1 ($163A) works out.

Works out where the far lane's distance marker stands: counts how many 480-unit stretches the scroll position holds, takes that stretch's 8 x 8 marker glyph from $17E4 (8 bytes each), shifts it right by the position's low three bits across two characters and writes them as characters $21 and $22 ($4908-$4917), with their screen columns in $16DA and $16DB.
marker1's two shifted characters (16 bytes), the scroll's low bits ($16D9) and the marker's two screen columns ($16DA, $16DB).
marker1's second shifted character.
marker1's scroll bits (0 to 7).
The far lane marker's first screen column.
The far lane marker's second screen column.
The near (lower) lane's divider row, worm two's (screen $42D0, row 18), as draw_lane1 does for the far lane, from $2918/$291A and $2914.
The near lane's distance marker, as marker1, into characters $23 and $24 ($4918-$4927), columns in $17E2 and $17E3.
marker2's two shifted characters, its scroll bits ($17E1) and screen columns ($17E2, $17E3).
marker2's second shifted character.
marker2's scroll bits (0 to 7).
The near lane marker's first screen column.
The near lane marker's second screen column.
The distance markers drawn into the dividers, 8 x 8 each: S for the start, then 1 to 9, then F for the finish, one for each 480-unit stretch, so the 100 metres are ten stretches of 48 units a metre.
The lane routines' work bytes: a copy of the far lane's offset ($183C/$183D), the offset being divided ($183E/$183F) and the stretch count ($1840).
The high byte of the copy of the near lane's offset.
The offset being divided, low byte.
The offset being divided, high byte.
How many 480-unit stretches the offset holds: which marker shows.
Blanks the screen, copies the stadium picture to the screen (1,024 character codes at $18A6, each plus $47) and its colours to colour RAM ($1C8E), waits 21 frames and turns the screen back on.

The stadium picture's character map, 40 x 25 (each code plus $47 when draw_stadium copies it): the panels and clock at the top, the stand and crowd, and the track. Its last 24 bytes are also the first 24 colours.
The stadium picture's character map, rows 6 to 12: the stand and the crowd.
The stadium picture's character map, rows 12 to 19: the bottom of the stand and the track with its two lanes.
The stadium picture's character map, rows 19 to 24 (the bottom of the track and the message row) and the 24 hidden bytes past the screen.
The stadium picture's colours, one byte a cell, copied into colour RAM by draw_stadium.
The stadium colours, rows 6 to 12: the stand and the crowd.
The stadium colours, rows 12 to 19: the track.
The stadium colours, rows 19 to 24, and the bytes past the screen.
Each worm's frame number, worm one then worm two; $FF hides the worm.
Worm two's frame number ($FF hides it).
Addresses of the 44 frame records set_worm_sprites reads.
The high bytes of the frame addresses, read as frame_table + 1.

Shows message A on the bottom row: first scrolls the old text off to the left, one character a frame, then, unless A is $FF, prints message A from the pointer table at $273F one letter at a time with a cursor block ($18) after it, each letter clicked through type_click ($26FB).
The typing sound: for any letter but a space, plays a short tone on voice 3 with the character code as its pitch (sawtooth, gate on), holds it, turns the gate off and waits. A and X are kept.
type_click's saved X.
Waits A x 256 calls of an empty routine.
delay's outer count.
Addresses of the eight messages show_message prints.
The high bytes of the message addresses, read as message_table + 1.

The eight bottom-line messages, each ended by $FF: 0 "WORM ONE READY PRESS FIRE", 1 "WORM TWO READY PRESS FIRE", 2 "PREPARE TO RACE", 3 "TIME LIMIT EXCEEDED RACE TERMINATED", 4 "COMPUTER PACE MAKER ON FAR TRACK", 5 "PRESS FIRE TO RACE AGAIN", 6 "KEYBOARD AND JOYSTICK TWO NOT ALLOWED", 7 "STOP TO QUIT ANY KEY TO CONTINUE".

Puts both worms in the idle state ($FF in $2927 and $2928) while the riders are asked to get ready.
Marks worm X's animation to stop at its next step ($80 in $2909).
Starts animation A for worm X ($290B): from its first step, running forwards, and starts the sound effect the table at $289A gives for it through play_effect ($2C48). X and Y are kept.
The sound effect start_anim plays for each of the eleven animations.

Advances worm X's animation when its hold count ($2911) runs out: forwards, backwards, or, when stopped, ends it ($FF); then shows the step's frame (anim_frame $28DA) and loads the hold count from the step.

Reads the current step of worm X's animation: the script's address from the table at $2940, four bytes a step. Byte 0 is the frame ($FF ends the script, marked by $290F = 0), byte 3 how many calls to hold it.

Each worm's state, two bytes to a variable, worm one first: animation stop flag ($2909), animation number ($290B), step ($290D), running flag ($290F), hold count ($2911), screen X ($2913) and Y ($2915), distance low and high ($2917, $2919), slime ($291B, up to $30), speed flag ($291D), race result ($291F: 0 racing, $80/$81 home, $82 out), speed ($2923), cooling level ($2925), state ($2927), controls ($2929), and the once-only press flags ($292B-$2938); then the six press timers ($2939-$293E) and the leader flag ($293F).
Each worm's animation number, worm one then worm two.
Each worm's animation step, worm one then worm two.
Each worm's animation running flag, worm one then worm two.

The leader flag: 0 when worm one leads, $FF when worm two does (camera).
Addresses of the eleven animation scripts anim_frame reads.
The high bytes of the animation script addresses, read as anim_table + 1.

The worms' eleven animation scripts, four bytes a step (frame, two spare bytes, hold count): each starts with a $FF step and ends with $FF. Animation 0 is the first; the table at $2940 gives each one's address.
Animation 1's script: a $FF step that marks the start, then frames 1, 7, 0, then $FF.
Animation 2's script: a $FF step that marks the start, then frames 0, 8, 2, 9, 3, 4, 10, 5, 6, 29, then $FF.
Animation 3's script: a $FF step that marks the start, then frames 11, 12, 13, 14, 1, then $FF.
Animation 4's script: a $FF step that marks the start, then frames 1, 17, 18, 17, 1, then $FF.
Animation 5's script: a $FF step, then its frames, then $FF.
Animation 6's script: a $FF step that marks the start, then frames 1, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, then $FF.
Animation 7's script, the longest, which st_burnt starts once animation 9 has ended: a $FF step, then its frames, then $FF.
Animation 8's script: a $FF step that marks the start, then frames 28, 27, 30, 31, then $FF.
Animation 9's script: a $FF step that marks the start, then frames 7, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38, then $FF.
Animation 10's script: a $FF step that marks the start, then frames 1, 7, 39, 40, 41, 42, 43, 38, then $FF.

Voice 1's finished flag.
Voice 2's finished flag.
Voice 3's finished flag, which countdown waits on.
Stops every sound effect: marks all three voices finished and silences the chip (sid_init), keeping A, X and Y. Nothing in this event calls it.
When the effects player is running ($2C12), checks whether all three voices have finished ($2C13-$2C15 all set) and silences the chip if so (sid_init $2F9A).
Starts sound effect A on voice X (0 to 2): unless another call is busy ($2CA4), points the voice's script at the effect's address from the table at $2CA5 and marks it playing ($2C13 + X cleared).
play_effect's voice ($2CA2), effect number ($2CA3) and busy flag ($2CA4).
play_effect's effect number.
play_effect's busy flag.

The high bytes of the effect addresses, read as effect_table + 1.
Addresses of the instruments, numbered from 1.
The high bytes of the instrument addresses, read as instrument_table + 1.
The instruments, seven bytes each: attack/decay, sustain/release, waveform, pitch slide low and high, slide rate, and a vibrato byte.
Instrument 1: attack/decay $00, sustain/release $F0, waveform $20.
Instrument 2: attack/decay $60, sustain/release $8A, waveform $80.
Instrument 3: attack/decay $80, sustain/release $A0, waveform $80.

Reads voice X's effect script at its saved pointer, with the I/O banked out while it reads: $FF ends the effect; $C0-$DF selects an instrument (low five bits); a byte under $80 is a note, followed by its length. A note sets the pitch from the frequency tables at $2FCC (low) and $300E (high), and a new instrument writes its attack/decay, sustain/release and waveform with the gate on, and its slide and vibrato settings.
Each voice's repeat flag for the effect scripts' $80-$83 control codes.
effect_read's note entry: the byte (less bit 7 set) is the note, the next its length; stores the script pointer back and sets the voice's pitch, and its instrument when it changed.
tick routine's saved voice number.
Steps the effect pointer at $15/$16 on one byte.
The ticks per note step ($2EF5), each voice's tick count ($2EF6-$2EF8) and slide count ($2EF9-$2EFB).
Each voice's tick count, one byte for each of the three voices.
Each voice's slide count, one byte for each of the three voices.

Once a frame, for each of the three voices: counts down the note's length, reads the next script entry when it ends, gates the note off one tick before, and slides the pitch by the instrument's step ($2D53/$2D56) every $2D59 ticks.
Each voice's register offset from $D400: 0, 7 and 14.
Writes 25 bytes from $2FB3 to the SID ($D400-$D418), which silences every voice, and marks all three voices as finished.
The 25 register values sid_init writes: every voice off, the volume at 15.
The notes' pitches, 66 low bytes ($2FCC) then 66 high bytes ($300E).
The notes' high bytes, the second half of note_table.
The last two of the notes' high bytes.

Reads the RUN/STOP key (keyboard row 7, column 7); when it is held, goes on to the quit prompt.
The NMI handler: returns at once, so RESTORE does nothing.

Leaves the event (RUN/STOP, and the NMI's way out): puts the best times ($0C2C-$0C2F, unless still $99) into the resident record at $B801-$B804 and the pace-maker flag into $B809, scores the championship ($B839) when $B800 says one is under way, banks the ROMs back in, resets the KERNAL's I/O, memory, vectors and screen, and loads the menu program HARRY ($316F). A failed load prints "ERROR READING DISK... ENSURE CORRECT DISK IS IN DRIVE", waits 200 frames and tries again; a good one sets $FF to 1 and jumps into the menu at $0E90.
The text quit_to_menu prints when HARRY will not load: clear screen, two returns, "ERROR READING DISK...", two returns, "ENSURE CORRECT DISK IS IN DRIVE", ended by $FF.
Loads "0:HARRY" (name at $319C) from drive 8 to its own address through the resident fast loader at $0800, reading the drive's status before and after. Returns carry set when the load failed.
The file name "0:HARRY" that load_harry asks for.
The per-frame update of both worms: reads the controls (read_controls $359D), then, for each worm, the computer's slither timing ($31B7) and the worm's state routine ($31DB).
For a worm whose speed flag $291D is clear, starts animation 4 and state 5 at the 4th and 9th second of each ten, once 0.05 seconds have passed.
Gives the worm back one unit of slime every 200 frames (up to $30) and runs the routine for its state ($2927 plus 1) from the address table at $3218.
The operand of the JMP at $3215, which worm_state rewrites with the state routine's address.
The high byte of the state routine address, second byte of the JMP's operand.

Addresses of the twelve worm state routines worm_state picks from (state plus 1): st_reset, st_bunched, st_stretch, st_slide, st_wait_down, st_bunch, st_hold, st_finish, st_burnt, st_anim_end, st_burnt2 and st_done.
The high bytes of the state routines' addresses, read as state_table + 1.
Worm state routine: stops the worm (speed $2923 zero), starts animation 3 and goes to state 1.

Worm state routine for a worm still racing. When press_up ($34DE) returns zero it acts: with right held (bit 3 of the controls $2929 clear) and 12 or more slime it makes the super-slither, speed $10 and animation 2, spending 12 slime and cooling the worm by 12 (up to $30); otherwise it adds 2 to the speed, at most 8, and starts animation 0 when the cooling level is $0C or more. Either way it clears the press flags and goes to the next state.
Worm state routine: steps the animation, and when the animation has ended and nothing holds it, goes back a state (when $292B is set) or on to the next.

Worm state routine while the worm slides with speed and down released: once per window ($292F), with fire held (bit 4 clear) and slime left, cools the worm by 4 (up to $30) and spends 2 slime; once per window ($2933) moves it on by its speed (move_worm $34BF) while the cooling level is $0C or more; and once per window ($2935) takes one off its speed and one off its cooling level, so a sliding worm heats up. With no speed left, or down pressed, it goes on to the next state.
Worm state routine: when press_down ($350F) returns zero, adds 2 to the speed (at most 8), starts animation 1, sets the speed flag $291D and goes to state 4.
Worm state routine: steps the bunching animation, moving the worm on while it is under $25 hot; when the animation ends, goes back a state or to state 0.
Worm state routine: steps the animation and, when it ends, goes to state 3; when down is pressed again, bunches up at once ($33A2).
Worm state routine for a worm that is out or has finished: state $82 (out) starts animation 9 and goes to state 8; state $84 has its own branch.
Worm state routine: steps the animation and, when it ends, starts animation 7 and goes to state 9.
Worm state routine: steps the animation and goes to state $0A when it ends.
Worm state routine: steps the animation and, when it ends, goes on as st_burnt does (animation 7, state 9).
Worm state routine end: sets state $0A, where the worm stays.
The RTS that ends st_done.
Adds a signed step to worm X's distance ($2917/$2919): the step is A, negated when its sign differs from the worm's speed ($2923).
move_worm's sign byte.

Decides whether worm X may stretch: returns A = 0 at once while up is held (bit 0 of $2929 clear); with up released, returns A = 0 when right is released or 12 or more slime is left, and otherwise, once per press window ($2937), takes one off the speed (not below 0) and returns zero as well. The caller acts on a zero result.

With down held (bit 1 of $2929 clear) returns A nonzero at once; with it released, once per press window ($2937) takes one off worm X's speed (not below 0) and returns zero. The caller acts on a zero result.
Counts down six timers and, when each runs out, re-arms one pair of the once-only press flags: $2937 every 10 frames, $2931 every 2, $2933 every 2, $2935 every 12, $292F every 10 and $292D every 200.

Reads both worms' controls into $2929 and $292A (read_device $35BB, $35C1), except that with one player ($0D62 not 2) worm one, the pace-maker on the far track, takes its controls from the script player at $3632. X is kept.

Reads worm one's controls from the device it chose ($0D60): joystick one ($DC01) or two ($DC00) as the port reads, a 0 bit for each direction or fire held; with right held, bit 1 (down) reads as released. Device 0, the keyboard, is read elsewhere ($35DE).
Worm two's controls, from its device $0D61, as read_device.
Reads the keyboard player's controls into the joystick's bit pattern: @ up, : down, K left, H right and the up-arrow key fire (keyboard rows 5, 3, 4 and 6), a 0 bit for each key held.
read_keys's work byte, where the bits are gathered.

The computer's pace-maker: every time its count ($3664) runs out, reads the next pair of the script at $3674 (frames to hold, controls to hold), skipping a super-slither entry (8) when worm one has under 12 slime, and returns the controls held, inverted into the joystick's 0-for-pressed bits. At the end of the script ($FF) it starts again from the first pair.
The pace-maker's frame count, held controls ($3665) and place in its script ($3666).
The pace-maker's held controls.
The pace-maker's place in its script.
Reached at the end of the pace-maker's script: loads Y with $16, which the next instruction (pacer_reset) at once replaces with 0, so the script restarts from its first pair.
Starts the pace-maker's script from its first entry ($3666 = 0) with its count run out ($3664 = 1), at the start of each race.
The pace-maker's script: pairs of (frames to hold, controls), the controls as bits (1 up, 2 down, 8 right, $10 fire), ended by $FF.

Places the two worms on the screen from the distance between them: within $87 units they are drawn either side of column $89, half the gap each way; further apart the leader is pinned at $CD and the other at $46. The leader goes on the right ($293F remembers which worm leads), and the screen X of each goes to $2913 and $2914.
Stores the two screen X positions for camera: the leading worm gets Y and the other X, whichever worm leads ($293F).
camera's work word: the distance between the worms.
camera_gap's high byte.
A copy of Space Hockey's program at the same addresses, left in the file by the build: nothing in this event reads it.
More of the leftover copy of Space Hockey, with its messages ("SECONDS OUT", "GAME ON", "DEMO MODE" and the rest) from $3B4C.
The last of the Space Hockey leftover, up to $3FFF.
